title: An Orc6 tether mediates ORC binding site switching during replication origin licensing
authors: David Driscoll; Larry J. Friedman; Jeff Gelles; Stephen P Bell
one_liner_zh: 该文通过单分子FRET研究ORC在复制起始许可中结合位点切换的拴系机制，涉及蛋白质-DNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，且方法为单分子生化而非AI或物理模拟，相关性有限。
abstract: During origin licensing, the origin recognition complex (ORC) loads two Mcm2-7 helicases onto DNA in a head-to-head conformation, establishing the foundation for subsequent bidirectional replication. Single-molecule experiments support a helicase-loading model in which one ORC loads both Mcm2-7 helicases at origins. For this to occur, ORC must release from its initial Mcm2-7 and DNA binding sites, flip over the helicase, and bind the opposite end of the Mcm2-7 complex and adjacent DNA to form the MO complex. Importantly, this binding-site transition occurs without ORC releasing into solution. Using a single-molecule FRET assay, we show that the N-terminal half of Orc6 tethers ORC to the N-terminal tier of Mcm2-7 (Mcm2-7N) during ORC’s binding-site transition. This interaction involves both the folded Orc6 N-terminal domain (Orc6N) and the adjacent unstructured linker and forms before ORC releases from its initial Mcm2-7 interaction. The absence of this interaction increases the rate of ORC release into solution, consistent with a tethering function. CDK phosphorylation of ORC inhibits the tethering interaction, providing a mechanism for the known CDK inhibition of MO complex formation. Interestingly, we identify mutations in the Orc6 linker region that support MO complex formation but prevent double-hexamer formation by inhibiting stable second Mcm2-7 recruitment. Our study provides a molecular explanation for a one-ORC mechanism of helicase loading and demonstrates that Orc6 is involved in multiple stages of origin licensing. Significance Statement Bidirectional DNA replication is critical for accurate and complete duplication of the genome. Eukaryotic organisms coordinate this through loading of two oppositely-oriented Mcm2-7 replicative helicases at origins of replication. Using single-molecule biochemical studies, we identified and characterized a tethering interaction during helicase loading that enables the helicase loader ORC (origin recognition complex) to flip between two Mcm2-7 and DNA binding sites to load the second helicases in the opposite orientation. This interaction is cell-cycle regulated as part of the mechanisms ensuring replication from a given origin initiates only once. Our findings have important implications for the multiple mechanisms of helicase loading and illustrate how single-molecule studies can complement structural studies to provide a full view of complex molecular assembly events.
abstract_zh: 在起始许可过程中，起始识别复合物（ORC）以头对头构象将两个Mcm2-7解旋酶装载到DNA上，为后续的双向复制奠定基础。单分子实验支持一种解旋酶装载模型，其中单个ORC在起始点装载两个Mcm2-7解旋酶。为实现这一点，ORC必须从其初始的Mcm2-7和DNA结合位点释放，翻转解旋酶，并结合Mcm2-7复合物的相对末端及相邻DNA以形成MO复合物。重要的是，这种结合位点转换发生在ORC不释放到溶液中的情况下。利用单分子FRET实验，我们展示了Orc6的N端一半在ORC结合位点转换过程中将ORC拴系到Mcm2-7的N端层（Mcm2-7N）。这种相互作用涉及折叠的Orc6 N端结构域（Orc6N）及相邻的无序连接区，并在ORC从其初始Mcm2-7相互作用释放之前形成。缺乏这种相互作用会增加ORC释放到溶液中的速率，这与拴系功能一致。CDK磷酸化ORC抑制拴系相互作用，为已知的CDK对MO复合物形成的抑制提供了机制。有趣的是，我们识别出Orc6连接区中的突变，这些突变支持MO复合物形成，但通过抑制稳定的第二个Mcm2-7招募来阻止双六聚体形成。我们的研究为解旋酶装载的单ORC机制提供了分子解释，并证明Orc6参与起始许可的多个阶段。**意义声明** 双向DNA复制对于基因组的准确和完整复制至关重要。真核生物通过在复制起始点装载两个相反方向的Mcm2-7复制解旋酶来协调这一过程。利用单分子生化研究，我们识别并表征了解旋酶装载过程中的一种拴系相互作用，该相互作用使解旋酶装载器ORC（起始识别复合物）能够在两个Mcm2-7和DNA结合位点之间翻转，以装载相反方向的第二个解旋酶。这种相互作用受细胞周期调控，作为确保给定起始点的复制仅启动一次的机制的一部分。我们的发现对解旋酶装载的多种机制具有重要意义，并展示了单分子研究如何补充结构研究，以提供复杂分子组装事件的完整视图。
